original_test_intent: Demonstrate the vendor-supported resilience or recovery behavior of a disposable NVMe M.2 device when SUT power is deliberately interrupted during the approved firmware commit/activation window, then verify the same device and system return to normal operation.
original_method: Use an owner-approved spare non-boot/data-free controller; bind exact model/serial/PCI/namespace identity; validate image/tool, commit action 3 slot 1, the precise interrupt trigger and recovery documentation; capture power and console timing; execute once only after explicit authorization; then prove same-device identity, expected prior/recovery firmware, namespaces, health, I/O and OS/service boot.
manual_activity: The storage/platform owner approves the disposable target, image/tool, commit semantics, exact interruption point, controlled power, recovery and maintenance; an operator observes console/power timing; the owner decides the verdict.
required_inputs: Disposable non-boot/data-free M.2 model, serial, controller, namespace and PCI identity
Current and expected prior/recovery FW revisions and slot map
Vendor-approved firmware image/tool/checksums and interruption/recovery documentation
Validated fw-commit slot 1 action 3 semantics and exact flashing/interruption observable
Controlled power and console/log capture with maintenance window
Backup/recovery image/media, vendor recovery/RMA plan and spare replacement
Explicit approvals for download, commit, timed power interruption and recovery
safety_requirements: Never use a boot, production, mounted or data-bearing drive
Do not replace the source stimulus with a guessed corrupt or wrong image
Verify exact target, image compatibility, commit semantics and vendor-supported interruption point
Use controlled power and console observation; prevent concurrent I/O
Capture full outputs, exit codes and interruption timestamps
Stop on controller disappearance, wrong identity/revision, boot failure or health/namespace anomaly
Do not retry download, commit, power cut or recovery automatically
agent_execution_scope: Perform read-only target, firmware, boot/mount/IO and health prechecks
Validate supplied artifacts and prepare the approved one-shot sequence
Execute download/commit and request or invoke the approved controlled power cut only with current explicit authorization
Collect complete post-reboot identity, revision, health, namespace, I/O and service evidence
Never choose the stimulus, target, image or timing, approve risk, retry failure or issue the DUT verdict
engineer_actions: Approve disposable target, valid image/tool, slot/action and vendor interruption timing
Approve controlled power, console, maintenance, backup and recovery/RMA plan
Authorize each destructive phase and issue PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED after complete recovery evidence

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: It recognizes a negative firmware case but changes intentional power interruption into corrupt-image rejection and uses invalid PARTIAL classification, so it does not cover the source.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: After every gate and approval, run the vendor-supported download and slot-1/action-3 commit on the verified spare, interrupt SUT power exactly at the approved observable point once, then stop on any unexpected post-reboot state.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Source /dev/nvme0 intent, slot 1, action 3, deliberate SUT power-cycle during flashing, post-reboot nvme list, Config-Check and 20/20-minute values remain; each literal requires owner validation.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use a disposable target and instrumented one-shot sequence with vendor-defined trigger, controlled power timing and comprehensive recovery verification.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds exact safeguards and measurable recovery evidence without replacing the deliberate interruption stimulus.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Clean corrupt-image rejection tests input validation, not resilience to loss of power during commit; they are not substitutes.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: The test can irreversibly brick the controller or prevent system boot even when performed correctly; recovery may require RMA.

project_override_considerations: If the vendor prohibits power interruption during action 3 or cannot define a safe observation point, this exact execution must remain unrun/blocked for owner disposition; a corrupt-image test may be added separately but cannot count as this case.
expected_evidence: Exact row/variant/hash and DeepSeek stimulus-change record
Owner approvals, disposable/non-boot proof and exact target identity with pre-test FW/health/namespace/mount/boot state
Image/tool checksums, vendor commit/interruption/recovery reference and approved trigger
Full download/commit output, controlled power/console timestamps and reboot trace
Same-device prior/recovery FW, namespace, health/error, I/O and OS/service evidence with unrelated-device audit
No-retry audit, recovery/RMA actions if any and owner PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The source mandates power loss during firmware flashing but provides no vendor-supported timing, disposable-target restriction, recovery path or complete normal-operation criteria. DeepSeek changes the test to corrupt-image rejection and uses invalid PARTIAL classification.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The static review is complete; execution is gated by potentially supplyable vendor method, disposable hardware, controlled power, recovery and explicit approvals. If the vendor forbids interruption, the engineer will disposition the case.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Functionality row 2042 Wistron-HW-00485-V002: approve a disposable non-boot/data-free M.2 target, vendor image/tool/checksum, fw-commit slot 1 action 3 semantics, exact supported interruption trigger and controlled power/console method, recovery/RMA plan, and measurable post-reboot identity/FW/health/namespace/I/O/OS criteria; confirm that corrupt-image rejection is a separate test and does not replace the source power-interruption stimulus.

review_improvement: Restores the exact destructive stimulus, rejects the corrupt-image substitution, makes one-shot authorization and halt behavior explicit, and expands `works normally` into traceable recovery evidence.
independent_technical_reasoning: Corrupt-image rejection happens before or outside a successful firmware commit and validates parser/signature safeguards; loss of power during commit validates atomicity or recovery, so the two failure modes are technically distinct. Because an interrupted commit can brick a controller and affect boot, only a disposable target under vendor-defined timing and controlled power is acceptable. Recovery cannot be inferred from `nvme list` alone; identity, revision, namespaces, health, I/O and system boot must all be verified.
